headline: Sensex Gains Over 500 Points Led by FMCG and Banking Stocks Amid FII Inflows

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) buying and fund inflows provided strong market support.
Gains in FMCG, banking, and consumer stocks propelled Sensex and Nifty higher.
BSE Insurance Index rose 1.15%, contributing to the positive sentiment.
US markets faced a sharp selloff overnight with Nasdaq plunging 2.2% and Dow dropping 700 points.
whatHappening: Sensex climbed over 500 points while Nifty approached the 25,300 mark.
Tata Motors PV plunged 8.7% after JLR cut its FY27 margin outlook.
Max Healthcare emerged as one of the top gainers during the session.
IBM announced plans to invest $3 billion annually in India as part of its global strategy.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices surged over 500 points supported by strong FMCG and banking gains alongside robust foreign fund inflows.
Tata Motors fell heavily by 8.7% after JLR trimmed its margin guidance, whereas Max Healthcare featured among the top gainers.
Overseas, US markets experienced significant declines with tech stocks dragging the Nasdaq down by 2.2%.
